Title: Mike McGlone Doubles Down On $10K Bitcoin Doom Call: 'Stock Bear Market Has Started'
Author: Anushka Basu   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 6:07 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T05:07:20+00:00
=== BODY ===
McGlone first predicted the decline in Q1 2025, when Bitcoin traded above $100,000, and said a 20% S&P 500 correction could start it.
The index is currently about 6% below its 52-week high.
Scott Melker said that the stock sell-off had not hit Bitcoin as hard as bears had expected.
Mike McGlone, Senior Commodity Strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, doubled down on his call for Bitcoin (BTC) to fall to $10,000, saying that he believes the next stock bear market has already started.
McGlone said he had first made the call in the first quarter of 2025, when Bitcoin traded above $100,000, and said that the outlook had remained unchanged.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
"The call from 1Q25 with Bitcoin above $100,000 was for it to lose a zero, on the back of a 20% drawdown in the S&P 500 (SPX) that stays down awhile, remains my base case," he wrote on X on Friday.
A Bitcoin price that "loses a zero" would fall about 90%, to roughly $10,000. McGlone said that level carried the weight for the asset, noting that "10,000 Bitcoin is a key pivot."
He also drew a link between crypto and stocks, saying that Bitcoin peaked on October 6 last year, while the Nasdaq peaked exactly a year later, on October 6, 2026.
"May the market gods be with us all when we have the next stock bear market. I think it has started," he said.
Bitcoin's price was trading at $75,830, up 0.2% during the past 24 hours, while the S&P 500 closed at 7,376 points on Friday, about 6% below its 52-week high of 7,844. That was well short of the 20% drop McGlone said would push Bitcoin toward $10,000.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin was in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it was at 'normal' levels over the past day.
McGlone's post came in response to crypto trader and well-known investor Scott Melker, famously known as the "Wolf of All Streets." He said that the stock sell-off had not hit Bitcoin as hard as bears had expected. "Nasdaq entered correction territory today, more than 10% below its recent high," Melker said on X.
Melker said the market had already covered half the drop that was meant to drag Bitcoin down. "The Nasdaq is down 10%, and we're still 17 or $18,000 above Bitcoin's low," he said.
"The case that the Nasdaq or the market dropping 20% would send Bitcoin to $10,000, to me, or something way lower right now does not make any sense because we're halfway there."

Title: What Sent Quanta Stock Lower?
Author: Trefis Team   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:28 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T01:28:51+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Shares of Quanta Services (PWR) fell 11.7% on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, as the S&P 500 gained 1.6%. The company released no announcements, earnings reports or regulatory filings on the day of the move or the day before. The drop occurred on a day when data center stocks sank after Democrats secured big wins in the US midterm elections. So what does Quanta, whose foundation is its utility business, have to do with data centers?
How Does Quanta's Work Reach Into Data Centers?
Quanta builds for data center customers alongside its work for utilities. Management said on the October 29 earnings call that the five largest technology companies will spend three times the capital budget of the utility side, adding that it likes Quanta's chances to grow there.
Management also said on the same call that Quanta works for the very best in the world at data centers, and that it cannot take on even 25% to 30% of the work those customers have in front of it. That data center work connects Quanta to the stocks that sank on November 4. Even so, its utility business, which management put at roughly $20 billion of the electric segment, remains the base of the company.
Did Quanta Fall Alone Or With Similar Companies?
Quanta fell alongside its peers. Every company on its Trefis peer list dropped during the same session, and two of them posted steeper declines than Quanta did. MasTec fell 15.4%, and Primoris Services dropped 14.0%. EMCOR, MYR and Dycom Industries fell by less.
Broad industrial stocks held up far better. XLI, the SPDR fund for the industrials sector, slipped 1.1% during the session as the S&P 500 rose. The selling hit Quanta's own group much harder than the wider sector.
Quanta had not fallen this far in a single session at any point in the prior 365 days. Its latest move of this size went the other direction, logging a 17.3% rise on July 30, 2026.
If you have owned the stock for a year, you remain ahead of the market. Quanta shares returned 32.4% over the past twelve months, compared with 14.9% for the S&P 500. The trajectory has turned downward since spring, however. The stock hit its highest close of the past year at $785.24 on May 6, 2026. Shares have lost 26.1% since then, while the S&P 500 gained 5.0%. Over the past month, from the October 2 close, the stock fell 14.2%, against a 0.4% dip for the S&P 500. The latest close of $580.44 is still well above the year's lowest close of $413.17 on January 8, 2026.
Based on sales, Quanta stock costs less than the broader market, trading at 2.3 times sales against 3.2 times for the S&P 500. On an earnings basis, however, the stock costs more, trading at 51.9 times against 22.8 for the S&P 500.
Signed contracts, including data center work, feed into Quanta's backlog, which stood at a record of about $64 billion at September 30. That backlog is the number to watch when the company reports its fourth-quarter 2026 results.

Title: Are You Sure You Understand Vertiv Stock's Risk?
Author: Trefis Team   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:05 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T01:05:25+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
From October 7 to November 5, 2026, Vertiv (VRT) stock fell 28.3%, compared with a 5.7% decline for the S&P 500. Peers Eaton and nVent Electric lost ground over those same dates, dropping 24.2% and 41.3% respectively, while a third peer, Emerson Electric, gained 2.1%. Vertiv's sales rose 61% from a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026, and holders may expect shares of a business growing that fast to hold up when the market turns. So how far have Vertiv shares fallen when the whole market fell?
Vertiv Stock Has Usually Fallen Further Than The Market
Across the six market shocks the company has traded through, Vertiv shares have fallen 36.9% on average, compared with a 16.8% drop for the S&P 500 over the same dates. During the 2020 COVID-19 crash, the stock fell 59%, while the index lost 34%. The 2025 US tariff shock saw the stock drop 45%, against 19% for the index. The summer-fall 2023 yield shock provided the one exception: Vertiv shares slipped 2.6% while the index shed 9.5%.
Each time, though, Vertiv shares have bounced back. At the median, the shares were back at their peak close 1.4 months after the low, and the longest wait was 12 months. At its November 5 close, the stock stood 53% below its highest close of the past year, which was set on May 14, 2026. That close was $176.73, and a repeat of the 36.9% average shock fall would take the shares to about $112.
Big falls hit the whole market too: the Nasdaq dropped 5.5% on November 5. Here's what came next the last 21 times.
Vertiv's Sales Are Growing Faster Than A Year Ago
Over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, Vertiv's sales grew 35.3% to $13.1 billion, outpacing the 28.8% growth from the twelve months before. Operating profit grew faster than sales during the third quarter of 2026, when the operating margin was 23.0%, up from 20.5% a year earlier.
Vertiv also held $3.71 billion of cash against $3.36 billion of debt on September 30, 2026. A year earlier, its $3.21 billion in debt exceeded its $1.94 billion of cash. On October 27, Vertiv paid about $1.45 billion in cash for UtilityInnovation Group, adding microgrid controls to its power and cooling portfolio. If that business meets its earnings targets over the next two years, Vertiv will pay up to $1.15 billion more. The upfront payment alone was larger than the amount by which cash exceeded debt on September 30.
What Vertiv's Management Flagged In October
On its October 28, 2026 call, management said that $100 million to $150 million of third-quarter sales had been delayed from the second quarter, meaning part of the third quarter's jump came from the quarter before.
Management also cited power availability, permitting and a shortage of skilled site labor as limits on the pace of data center building, but said they are not slowing Vertiv's growth. Management added that a large increase in capacity in the Americas during the second half is bringing some inefficiency there.
Leaving out acquisitions, third-quarter orders more than doubled from a year earlier, management said, and on the same call it said Vertiv will stop sharing orders data. With orders no longer reported, Vertiv's fourth-quarter net sales are the figure to watch against its guide of $4.31 billion to $4.51 billion when the company reports in February 2027.

Title: The S&P 500 Just Fell More Than 4% in a Day From Near Its Record. Here's What Happened Next in 2 Similar Situations Since 1950.
Author: Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 3:43 AM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T02:43:02+00:00
=== BODY ===
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 4.36% on Thursday, Nov. 5, ending at 7,353.73. It was the index's worst day since April 4, 2025, when it lost nearly 6%.
What made Thursday's drop unusual was where it started. The index had closed Wednesday at 7,688.62, under 2% off its record close of 7,818.93 on Oct. 6.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
Tech shares led the way down, and chip stocks fell hardest, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index losing around 12%.
Two poor chipmaker reports and a midterm election that had investors nervous about new limits on artificial intelligence data centers both hurt the group.
I wanted to check how rare this mix is. Looking through Yahoo Finance's daily closing prices (dividends left out), I counted 56 earlier days since 1950 when the S&P 500 dropped 4% or more. Only two of them began with the index within 2% of a record close. One was Sept. 26, 1955, and the other was Oct. 13, 1989.
The 1955 drop was on the first trading day after word of President Dwight Eisenhower's heart attack. The S&P 500 had closed at a record the Friday before, and it fell around 6.6% that Monday.
The year that followed went pretty smoothly. A month later, the index was flat. It was up around 6% after three months and about 13% after six.
And a year after the drop (252 trading days), it was up about 7%. Even its lowest close in that time was only about 4% below where it ended on Sept. 26.
The 1989 drop came on a Friday the 13th. That day, the group behind a $6.75 billion labor-management buyout of UAL, the parent of United Airlines, couldn't get enough financing. The S&P 500 fell around 6.1% that day, from about 1.2% below the record close it set on Oct. 9.
The year that followed was rockier. The index was up around 2% a month later and about 3% after six months. But it was down about 10% a year after the drop, as the economy slipped into the 1990-1991 recession. At its lowest close over that year, the index was around 11% below its Oct. 13 level.
In short, the two closest matches split. Two cases can't say much by themselves.
The broader record looks a lot better. Of the 56 earlier drops of 4% or more since 1950, 47 were followed by a higher index 12 months on, with a median gain of around 23%. And the odds improved the longer investors waited. The index was up a month later in 36 of the 56 cases, after three months in 41, after six months in 43, and after a year in 47.
Of course, most of these drops came in very different conditions. In 47 of the 56 cases, the index was already at least 10% below its record when the drop hit, and the typical one started around 24% below it. Over a third of them (21) came during 2008 and 2009 alone.
This 23% median gain, then, mainly reflects rebounds from deep in sell-offs that were already well underway. Thursday's drop started from near the peak.
Limit the list to drops that began within 5% of a record, and five cases are left (1955, 1986, 1989, 1997, and 2018). Four of the five were up a year later. But the median gain was around 7%, well below the full group's.
Sure, five cases is still a tiny sample. But I think it's a fair reminder that the largest rebounds in this record followed much bigger falls than the one investors just saw.
Even after Thursday, the S&P 500 is up around 7% in 2026 as I write, and it's about 6% off its Oct. 6 record. Its price-to-earnings ratio, at around 25, is also far above its long-term median of about 15.
In the end, this history doesn't point in one direction. And the wider record arguably looks strong partly because most of its big drops started from much lower levels.
I wouldn't sell an S&P 500 index fund over Thursday's drop. For a buy-and-hold investor, selling after a 4% day has usually meant missing what came next, as 47 of the 56 earlier cases were up a year later.
But I also wouldn't count on a 20%-plus rise from here just because so many past drops were followed by one. Starting this close to a record, and at that valuation, the lower gain after 1955 or even the loss after 1989 might be the more realistic guide.

Title: What Does The Market Want From Boeing Stock?
Author: Trefis Team   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:15 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T01:15:30+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Boeing (BA) stock fell 26.4% from August 7 to November 5, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 5.0%. The price appears to want a steadier 737 factory, and management said on October 27 that it does not expect steady output at 47 jets a month until 2027. Yet management credited third-quarter sales growth mainly to defense and services, not jetliners. That is the mismatch, though defense helps only if it keeps growing at a real profit. So how fast is Boeing's defense business growing?
Boeing's Defense Sales Grew 15% In The Third Quarter
Defense revenue rose 15% to $7.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, while Boeing's jetliner sales shrank. Over the same quarter, revenue from its jetliners fell 3% to $10.7 billion. Management attributed that decline to a less favorable mix of deliveries. That makes defense about a third of Boeing's $24.2 billion in quarterly sales.
Management credited the defense rise mainly to higher volume, including classified missile and weapons programs. It said about 2 points of the increase came from Spirit, which contributed about $150 million of the unit's sales in the quarter. Orders are running well ahead of sales. The defense unit booked $23 billion of orders in the quarter, and management put its backlog at a record $101 billion. That backlog does not yet include the US Navy's next fighter jet, which the Navy selected Boeing to design, build and deliver.
Management also expects more defense growth than it did a year ago, forecasting revenue growth in the middle single digits or higher going forward, compared with the low single digits it was thinking of then. That is still slower than the third quarter's 15%, about 2 points of which came from Spirit.
Does Boeing's Defense Business Earn Enough Yet?
Not yet. On management's own measure, the defense unit's operating margin was 6.2% in the third quarter, and that figure includes a $252 million gain on the sale of HRL Laboratories. That gain accounted for about half the unit's operating profit; without it, the margin would have been about 3%. Management said it remains confident of reaching high single-digit margins, so the profit is still catching up with the sales.
That matters because the jetliners are where Boeing loses money. On the same measure, the jetliner unit's operating margin was negative 6.5%. Management also expects 737 deliveries for 2026 to come in shy of its 500 target, because the factory is taking longer to steady.
Defense answers part of that worry: it earns a profit while the jetliners do not, and its sales are growing while theirs shrink. But its margin is thin, and Boeing as a whole still reported a net loss of $116 million in the third quarter.
What Could Go Wrong For Boeing's Defense Business?
You cannot yet see from the record backlog how much profit the new programs will earn. Management said it could not say what type of contract the Navy fighter is under, only that it is an appropriate contract type. The new work also costs cash first. Management listed around $1 billion of higher capital spending, including growth tied to recent defense awards, among the items weighing on free cash flow in 2027.
If defense growth slows, Boeing's growth falls back on its jetliners, where the 737 factory is still steadying. If the defense margin stays thin, defense adds sales without adding much profit.
Defense is still growing faster than the jetliners, but its profit is less settled, since the third-quarter margin included a one-time gain. Boeing is expected to report in January 2027, and the defense unit's operating margin is the number to watch then.

Title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Rose 5% in the Market’s Worst Week Since April 2025
Author: Jeremy Phillips   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:00 AM GMT+1 7 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T03:00:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Berkshire Hathaway's Class B shares gained 5% in the market's worst week since April 2025 while the company sat on about $365 billion in cash.
Weeks as bad as this one preceded a higher market a year later 71% of the time, with a median gain of 14%.
A retiree with $900,000 can borrow the idea by parking three years of withdrawals, about $108,000, in Treasury bills so downturns never force stock sales.
The stock market just had its worst week since April 2025. The S&P 500 index fund fell 2.7% from last Friday's close to this one, dragged down by Thursday's 4.4% selloff in artificial intelligence stocks. The same week, the Class B shares of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway rose 5.2% and set a record closing high on Wednesday.
Berkshire reports its third-quarter results on Saturday morning, and the number most investors will check first is how much cash it is holding. At the end of June it had about $365.5 billion, roughly 29% of the company's entire market value, according to CNBC.
If you are 67, retired, and have $900,000 saved with 60% in stocks, this week cost you about $14,500. You also collect $2,800 a month from Social Security. Here is what Berkshire's habit of keeping cash on hand looks like when you apply it to your own savings.
Buffett stepped down as Berkshire's chief executive at the start of 2026 and is now its chairman. Greg Abel runs the company. The cash habit is Buffett's, and Abel has only started to spend some of it.
Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.
Buffett has explained the idea for decades: cash lets you act when prices fall, and it means you never have to sell something good at a bad moment to pay a bill. Berkshire keeps most of its cash in short-term Treasury bills, which pay about 4.2% today.
The habit has started to pay off. In the second quarter, Berkshire was a net buyer of stocks after 14 straight quarters of net selling, putting nearly $20 billion to work, and it bought back about $4.5 billion of its own shares. Its operating earnings rose 16% to $12.98 billion.
On Saturday, watch two things. Did the cash pile shrink again, which would mean Berkshire is finding things to buy? And was it a net buyer of stocks for a second straight quarter, going into a selloff like this one?
The S&P 500 index fund has daily prices going back to late 1999, which covers 1,408 weeks. Only 119 of them were as bad as this week's 2.7% drop or worse.
After those 119 weeks, the fund was higher one year later 85 times, or 71% of the time. The median gain over the next year was 14.3%. The worst result came after a bad week in March 2008, when the fund was still down 47.5% a year later, in the middle of the financial crisis. The best came after March 2020, when it was up 71.6% a year later.
Most of the time, a week like this one was followed by a better year. Some of the time, it was the start of something far worse. Nobody can tell you in advance which one this is, and that uncertainty is exactly what the cash is for.
You do not need $365 billion to use the same idea. You need enough cash to cover the money you plan to spend over the next few years, so a falling market never forces you to sell stocks at a low.
Here is how it works for the 67-year-old with $900,000:
Annual withdrawal: 4% of $900,000 is $36,000 a year, or $3,000 a month.
Total monthly income: $3,000 from savings plus $2,800 from Social Security is $5,800 a month.
The cash bucket: three years of withdrawals is $108,000, about 12% of the portfolio.
What it earns: at a 4.21% Treasury bill rate, $108,000 pays about $4,550 a year in interest.
With that bucket in place, a further 20% drop in stocks would knock about $108,000 off the $540,000 stock portion. That is a painful paper loss. It would not change what you spend for the next three years, and it gives the stock portion time to recover before you need to sell any of it.
The worst way to build a cash bucket is to dump stocks in the middle of a bad week. There are better ways to get there:
Use the bond and cash portion first. Most 60/40 portfolios already hold more than three years of spending outside stocks. If yours holds $360,000 in bonds and cash, moving $108,000 of it into Treasury bills or a money market fund takes care of the bucket without selling a single share.
Refill it in good years. In years when stocks are up, sell enough to top the bucket back up to three years. In years when they are down, spend from the bucket and leave the stocks alone.
Let dividends flow into it. Turning off dividend reinvestment on your stock funds sends that cash straight into the bucket.
Cash is safe, and it has a cost. Over long stretches, stocks have earned more than Treasury bills, so a bigger cash bucket means a smaller long-run portfolio. Three years is a common middle ground. Two years leaves you more exposed to a long slump, and five years gives up more growth.
Treasury bill rates also change. If the Federal Reserve cuts rates, the 4.21% on your bucket will fall, and so will Berkshire's interest income on its own pile.
Stocks just had their worst week since April 2025, and Buffett's Berkshire went up while holding about $365 billion in cash, around 29% of its value. When it reports on Saturday, its cash pile will show whether it saw the selloff as a chance to buy. For a 67-year-old with $900,000 and $2,800 a month from Social Security, the same idea means keeping about $108,000, three years of withdrawals, in Treasury bills earning roughly $4,550 a year, so a bad week never turns into a forced sale.

Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) remain under pressure due to a U.S. market rout. Bitcoin's price was trading sideways at $75,000 U.S. on Nov. 6, its lowest level since late August. Ethereum (CRYPTO: $ETH) was also down and trading at $2,200 U.S. after digital assets were pulled lower amid a market selloff over the past week.
Every corner of the U.S. market plunged on Nov. 5 as investors grow increasingly worried about the artificial intelligence (A.I.) trade. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 1,800 points on the day and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index dropped 5.5% and entered a correction.
The market crash hit digital assets that were already reeling from the $6.3 billion U.S. theft at crypto exchange Binance. There are also concerns about the future of the Clarity Act legislation after the left-leaning Democratic Party won control of the U.S. Congress in midterm elections. The Binance hack and fate of the Clarity Act are hurting sentiment towards crypto, say analysts.
NYSE Parent ICE to Bring Hyperliquid-Based Perpetual Futures to US
Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Price Forecast To $1.6 Million By 2036
Survey Finds 90% Of Large Businesses Are Embracing Tokenized Money
Moody's Assigns Investment-Grade Rating To Ripple's Stablecoin
Stablecoin Firm RedotPay To Hold IPO By Year's End: Reports
Here's what else happened with cryptocurrencies over the past week…
Binance Withdrawals Top $10 Billion: Customer withdrawals from Binance accelerated to $10.97 billion U.S. days after the crypto platform experienced a massive theft. Binance clients pulled nearly $11 billion U.S. in crypto and cash from the trading exchange after it resumed withdrawals on Nov. 1. Investors fled Binance following a record breaking $6.3 billion U.S. hack of the platform on Oct. 30. U.S. authorities say North Korea was behind the theft.
Tether Owns $11.5 Billion Worth Of Bitcoin: Leading stablecoin provider Tether (CRYPTO: $USDT) reported owning 150,000 Bitcoin worth $11.50 billion U.S. The Bitcoin holdings were disclosed as part of the company's latest report on the reserves backing its USDT stablecoin. Tether also reported having more than 730 million users of its stablecoin worldwide and an average 30 million digital wallets that hold USDT coin.
Circle Cuts 5% Of Workforce: Stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (NYSE: $CRCL) has announced plans to cut 5% of its workforce. The company announced the job cuts along with its third-quarter financial results, attributing a $9.1 million U.S. restructuring charge to the headcount reduction. Circle Internet Group had 1,100 full-time employees at the start of this year. The 5% workforce reduction would eliminate about 55 workers.
Strategy Resumes Bitcoin Buying: Serial cryptocurrency acquirer Strategy (NASDAQ: $MSTR) resumed its purchases of Bitcoin, adding 811 of the digital tokens to its holdings over the past week. The company led by Chairman Michael Saylor bought 811 Bitcoin for $65.5 million U.S. at an average price of $80,846 U.S. between Oct. 26 and Nov. 1. Strategy's holdings now stand at 849,327 BTC worth $65.9 billion U.S. The previous week, Strategy had paused its Bitcoin buying leading into the company's quarterly financial results.
BitGo Launches Institutional Trading Business: Crypto infrastructure firm BitGo Holdings (NYSE: $BTGO) launched a new institutional trading and financial solutions business. Called "BitGo Global Markets," the new business brings together global liquidity, execution, financing, derivatives, and settlement services, according to the company. The new institutional trading division is being led by former NYDIG executive Pete Janney following BitGo's acquisition of NYDIG's institutional and trading business earlier this year.
Bitmine Resumes Stock Buybacks: Bitmine Immersion Technologies (NYSE: $BMNR) is ramping up its stock buybacks as it nears its goal of owning 5% of Ethereum's circulating supply. Bitmine resumed its share repurchases at the end of October after a 10-week pause. The Ethereum treasury firm bought 2.04 million of its own shares over the past week at an average price of $22.48 U.S., spending about $45.9 million U.S. total on the buybacks. It was Bitmine's first share repurchase of any kind since Aug. 17 of this year.
Morgan Stanley Tokenizes U.S. Equities: Investment bank Morgan Stanley (NYSE: $MS) moved quickly to tokenize U.S. equities following the launch of new tokenization infrastructure on Wall Street. Morgan Stanley is among the first banks to use the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation's new tokenization infrastructure to tokenize popular U.S. stocks. Digital versions of stocks can be traded around the clock and offer faster settlement times, according to advocates. On social media, Morgan Stanley said that it has tokenized both U.S. stocks and government Treasury bonds.
Bitcoin ETFs See $430 Million Of Outflows: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that track the spot price of Bitcoin experienced $430 million U.S. of outflows on Nov. 5 as equity markets melted down. The heavy outflows were led by leading Bitcoin ETFs managed by Fidelity Investments and BlackRock (NYSE: $BLK). Investors pulled money from the ETFs as Bitcoin's price fell more than 5% to $75,000 U.S. For the week ended Nov. 5, about a dozen U.S.-listed Bitcoin ETFs saw cumulative outflows of $869.8 million U.S.
Hut 8 Stock Plunges On Poor Financial Results: The stock of Hut 8 (NASDAQ: $HUT) fell as much as 18% on Nov. 4 after the Bitcoin miner turned data centre operator posted poor quarterly financial results. Hut 8 posted an earnings per share (EPS) loss of -$1.23 U.S., which was worse than the loss of -$1.06 U.S. that had been expected on Wall Street. Revenue of $71.07 million U.S. was below the consensus analyst estimate of $75.8 million U.S. The company, which is building data centres to run A.I. models, also said that its loans and liabilities grew to $7.41 billion U.S. as of Sept. 30 this year.
Brazil's Largest Crypto Exchange Hit By Theft: Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said it was hit by a security incident that cost it $46.3 million U.S. in lost assets. The exchange said the incident did not affect customers or result in a data breach. The company also published the digital wallet addresses where the stolen crypto is headed to help security firms track the digital assets. Mercado Bitcoin's hack occurred days after the record $6.3 billion U.S. theft at Binance.

Title: Wall Street stocks rally after heavy AI-related selloff
Author: By Chibuike Oguh and Marc Jones   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:39 PM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T22:39:19+00:00
=== BODY ===
NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Wall Street equities mostly rallied on Friday, reversing course after trillions of dollars of world stock market value were wiped out over fears that Democratic election victories this week ‌would bring tighter US regulations for the AI industry.
The benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq finished higher, with technology, communication ‌services and industrials stocks driving gains. The Dow ended lower. All three indexes notched weekly losses following a brutal selloff in the prior session.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell ​0.46%, the S&P 500 rose 0.31%, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.1%.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was up 4.2% after slumping in its biggest one-day drop since April 2025. Nvidia rose nearly 3%, after its worst day since January 2025, when the emergence of low-cost Chinese AI model DeepSeek hammered markets.
Other heavyweight chipmakers, including AMD, Intel, and Micron Technology, closed up between 5% and 11%, while Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX were also up 4% ‌and nearly 9% respectively after losses earlier this ⁠week.
"Most of the disruption of the AI buildout will not probably occur but it's just the uncertainty of the change in government from Republican-led to Democratic-led, not only at the federal level but the state, local ⁠levels," said Gerry Sparrow, president and portfolio manager at Sparrow Capital Management.
"That's causing some disruption in the expectations of investors ... The volatility around elections or any political event, whether it be war or terrorist attack, is always going to disrupt the market."
Texas' Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said on Thursday that the ​state — ​which already has a large share of US data centres — will introduce new ​laws to protect local communities from their further mass ‌buildup.
The jitters are hitting an AI trade already under pressure from fears that the massive cost of the data centres and other infrastructure will limit future returns, spurring margin calls and spooking retail investors and hedge funds alike.
The bounces were in stark contrast with market action in the rest of the world. Europe's STOXX 600 lost 1%. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI both slumped about 6%. For the Nikkei — just like Wall Street the previous day — it was the biggest one-day drop since US President Donald Trump's "Liberation Day" trade tariff ‌panic of April 2025.
The MSCI All-World index fell 0.68% while MSCI's broadest index of ​Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan lost nearly 3%.
US nonfarm payrolls, usually one ​of the most-watched pieces of data, but largely overshadowed by the ​tech drama, showed a stronger-than-expected 165,000 pickup in jobs.
An anticipated slowdown in annual wage growth to below 3% ‌for the first time in nearly 5-1/2 years did ​not materialise either, as it came ​in at 3.1%.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note ticked up to 4.86%, having dropped to its lowest level since September 9 overnight.
In currencies, the dollar rose against major currencies including the euro, yen and Swiss franc. It was up 0.52% ​against the yen and rose 0.47% against the ‌Swiss franc. The euro was down 0.68% against the dollar at $1.1142.
Brent crude prices settled at $98.32, rising just 0.03%, on hopes ​the midterms' results might prompt Trump to de-escalate the Iran war.
Spot gold was flat at $4,066.28 per ounce.
(Reporting by Chibuike ​Oguh in New York; Editing by Jonathan Spicer, Chizu Nomiyama, Rod Nickel)

Title: Warren Buffett Says This 1 Investing Move Is Key After a Midterm Election. History Says He's Right.
Author: Katie Brockman, The Motley Fool   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 12:20 AM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T23:20:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
It's been a rough week for the stock market.
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) and Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES: ^DJI) recently experienced their worst day in over a year. The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) fared even worse, falling nearly 12% from its October high and entering a technical correction.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
Much of the volatility stems from AI stocks, as concerns around their sustainability mount. With Democrats sweeping Congress in this week's midterm elections, many investors are concerned that stricter regulations may slow the data center build-out and negatively affect stocks spending heavily on AI infrastructure.
While nobody can say where the market is headed in the coming weeks, Warren Buffett has some timeless advice on how political uncertainty should affect your investment strategy.
In Berkshire Hathaway's 2018 annual shareholder letter, published in early 2019, Buffett offered some words of wisdom on investing during high-tension political periods.
At the time, the U.S. was in a similar political boat as today. The 2018 midterms had occurred just a few months prior, when Democrats took control of the House of Representatives and ended the Republican trifecta during President Trump's first term.
Also similar to today, all three major market indexes sank in the week following the elections.
However, Buffett's advice for investing during politically charged eras is simple: continue buying quality stocks. The market will thrive over time regardless of who is president, and the wisest investors look past volatility and bet on strong businesses.
"Our country's almost unbelievable prosperity has been gained in a bipartisan manner," he noted in the Berkshire letter.
"Since 1942, we have had seven Republican presidents and seven Democrats. In the years they served, the country contended at various times with a long period of viral inflation, a 21% prime rate, several controversial and costly wars, the resignation of a president, a pervasive collapse in home values, a paralyzing financial panic and a host of other problems. All engendered scary headlines; all are now history."
The market's short-term performance will always be volatile to some degree, but what really matters is how it recovers over time.
While the market was shaky in the days following the 2018 elections, the S&P 500 has soared by more than 200% since then -- despite experiencing the COVID-19 crash and 2022 bear market in that time. If you'd invested in an S&P 500 ETF on Election Day 2018, you'd have more than tripled your money by today.
If we're on the cusp of a bear market, stock prices could plunge yet again. Yet the healthiest companies will not only pull through, but go on to experience lucrative returns over the coming years.
In Berkshire's 2018 letter, Buffett outlined his and then-business partner Charlie Munger's investing strategy:
"Charlie and I have no idea as to how stocks will behave next week or next year. Predictions of that sort have never been a part of our activities. Our thinking, rather, is focused on calculating whether a portion of an attractive business is worth more than its market price."
Quality stocks with robust underlying fundamentals are the most likely to thrive over time, and loading up on those stocks now can protect your portfolio against even the most severe volatility.
During the dot-com bubble, for example, the companies that fell apart were those with unsustainable business models, weak competitive advantages, or inexperienced leadership teams. But plenty of stocks survived, even if the short term was rocky.
Amazon sank by nearly 95% between 1999 and 2001, for instance. Nvidia crashed by more than 87% in 2002 alone. And Apple lost more than 51% of its value in a single trading day in 2000. Investors who held on to those stocks back then, however, would have built life-changing wealth by today.
If history proves just one thing, it's that buying quality companies with solid fundamentals and then holding those stocks for years (or, ideally, decades) is the most effective way to hedge against volatility.
The market's short-term performance can be daunting, and if you're feeling rattled by all the recent turbulence, that's normal. But with a solid portfolio full of long-term investments, you'll be well-positioned for whatever may come next.

Title: 5 Best 52-Week Low NASDAQ Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires
Author: Farooq   Sat, November 7, 2026 at 5:05 AM GMT+1 9 min read
Published: 2026-11-07T04:05:30+00:00
=== BODY ===
Scan the Nasdaq stocks hitting 52-week lows this week and a pattern jumps out: many of the biggest names build, power or rent space for artificial intelligence. Few of these businesses are shrinking. Several reported record revenue in recent weeks, and their shares kept sliding anyway.
The reason has less to do with earnings than with money and politics, and both turned sharply worse over the past month.
The first shock came from the bond market. CRWV has taken on more than $51 billion of debt and obligations to build its AI infrastructure, CNBC reported on October 15. By October 21, CNBC said, its shares were down 36% for the month, and the spread on its five-year credit default swaps, a measure of the cost of insuring its debt, had reached 1,145 basis points. Barclays credit analyst Andrew Keches told clients that sentiment toward AI bonds was "decidedly negative."
Readers weighing the pullback can read our analysis of whether CRWV's recent drop is a buying opportunity.
More pressure followed. Elon Musk said more than 200 neoclouds, the companies that rent out AI computing power, would see "guppy-level death and consolidation," CNBC reported on October 26. Two days later, Microsoft reported capital spending below analyst estimates and said some third-party capacity it expected had been delayed, CNBC reported on October 28. Neocloud stocks fell again.
Then came the election. Reuters reported on November 4 that Wall Street closed sharply higher after Democrats won Congress, but data center shares fell on fears of tighter AI regulation. Democrats made gains in Texas and Georgia, where public opposition to the industry's rapid expansion has been growing.
The market split in two. Shares of cash-rich AI heavyweights rose, while chipmakers and data center operators fell: Hut 8 lost 23%, IREN 11%, Core Scientific 10% and Applied Digital 6.7%. Citi Research's head of US equity strategy, Scott Chronert, said any change in the pace of the buildout alters the outlook for many of those suppliers.
We also wrote about how leverage turned an AI bet into a fire sale for one fund.
The pressure carried into the next day. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data center capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses, Reuters reported on November 5. Large technology companies, by contrast, rose on the view that a slower buildout would curb their own spending, Reuters said.
We just shared the expanded list of 10 Best 52-Week Low NASDAQ Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires here. You can find the top 5 stocks below.
For this article, we used Finviz to screen for NASDAQ-listed stocks that hit a new 52-week low as of November 5, 2026. We then checked how many of the 107 billionaires we track held each stock as of Q2 2026, and ranked the 10 with the most billionaire holders in ascending order. We also list each stock's number of hedge fund holders as of Q2 2026, from our database of 1,006 hedge funds.
INNIO's stock tumbled after the best quarter in its history. The company makes the gas engines that let a data center generate its own power instead of waiting years for a grid connection, so a slower buildout hits it directly. Reutersreported that UBS analysts estimate about 30% of expected US data center capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from construction pauses, a worry that grew once Democrats won Congress.
The bulls' case sits in the order book. Revenue rose 57% to a record $1.2 billion, and the equipment backlog reached $8.0 billion, with most of the growth coming from data center deliveries. Management raised its full-year outlook. Chief executive Olaf Berlien said the company is scaling capacity to meet accelerating demand for AI infrastructure, and a 620-megawatt follow-on order from a data center developer came in during the quarter. Bulls add that even if some projects pause, a backlog of that size gives the company a long runway of deliveries already committed.
For more on who is buying those engines, see our piece on a 450-megawatt order for INNIO's gas engines.
Cerebras fell after a single report. Research firm SemiAnalysis said OpenAI would run the "Ultrafast" mode of its newest model on Nvidia chips instead of Cerebras hardware, and CNBC reported that the stock dropped nearly 20% that week, to its lowest since the May IPO, as insider lockups expired and more shares reached the market. OpenAI is a large piece of Cerebras's future, so the news stung. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman soon responded by calling Cerebras a close partner.
Bulls lean on what is already contracted. At the end of June, Cerebras held $25.4 billion in contracted work still to be delivered, and its core revenue of $209.9 million more than doubled from a year earlier. Its cloud business grew 287%, and management said it plans to more than triple revenue in 2027. AWS, AMD and CrowdStrike are among its customers and partners, which widens the list beyond OpenAI. Bulls add that Altman's response suggests the relationship with its biggest customer remains intact despite the headline.
That backlog is the subject of our look at how Cerebras could turn it into high-margin growth.
CoreWeave's problem is the price of money, not a lack of customers. The company rents out Nvidia chips and has taken on more than $51 billion of debt and obligations to build capacity. Bond yields near 15% and a jump in the cost of insuring that debt helped drive the stock down 36% in October, CNBC reported. Neocloud shares, which Reuters called a barometer of worry over AI spending, slid again after the midterm elections.
Bulls keep pointing to what customers have already signed. Second-quarter revenue rose 112%, and revenue backlog stood at about $104 billion, a figure that left out more than $25 billion in new commitments added early in the third quarter. Nvidia, which supplies the chips, also invested in the company in January. Management raised its 2026 revenue forecast, so the debate now is how fast those contracts can turn into cash. Bulls add that the backlog gives lenders something concrete to underwrite, which they argue should ease the funding pressure over time as customers begin paying.
Whether that balance sheet can carry the load is a question we explored for CoreWeave.
Core Scientific touched a 52-week low on the very day it reported third-quarter results. The company is turning former bitcoin mines into data centers that lease power and space to AI customers, and that conversion eats cash. Capital spending reached $985.1 million in the quarter. When data center stocks tumbled after the midterm elections, Core Scientific fell 10%, Reuters reported.
The bulls' answer is that the spending is turning into revenue. Colocation revenue jumped nearly 60% from the prior quarter to $215.4 million, and adjusted EBITDA more than tripled. The company is billing for 485 megawatts of capacity. Chief executive Adam Sullivan said the first colocation agreement is nearing full delivery while construction under a second is underway across five campuses, so contracted capacity still to be delivered keeps the growth going. Bulls add that this scale of billable capacity shows the conversion strategy works in practice, not only on paper. They argue that heavy spending is the price of getting capacity online, and that revenue from leases is now starting to catch up with the outlay.
We recently looked at why Core Scientific keeps buying more power.
Sterling Infrastructure delivered a record quarter and still watched its shares fall, which says a lot about where investor worry sits right now. The company clears land and does the electrical work for data centers, chip plants and factories, so its fortunes follow the AI buildout. Reuters reported that when Democrats won Congress, with gains in Texas and Georgia where opposition to data centers has been growing, operators and suppliers of the buildout sold off on fears of a slower pace.
Bulls say the business itself has not changed. Third-quarter revenue rose 127%, and combined backlog, which includes awards not yet signed, reached $6.14 billion. Management raised its 2026 outlook and counts nearly $8 billion of scoped work once the next phases of current projects are included, which it says gives years of visibility. Chief executive Joe Cutillo credited strong demand and disciplined execution for the results. Bulls add that a backlog of that size, paired with a raised outlook, suggests the pullback reflects sentiment rather than the work in hand.
Our ranking of the best AI infrastructure stocks to hold for the long term covers more of the group.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA) on 6 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Fahrenheit. The qualifying value is converted using °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 and rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Fahrenheit value determines which range contains it. For example, 18.3°C is 64.94°F and counts as 65°F; 17.8°C is 64.04°F and counts as 64°F; 19°C is 66.2°F and counts as 66°F; −22.5°C is exactly −8.5°F and counts as −8°F.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

markets.description:
This market will resolve in favor of the player that finishes the 2026-27 NBA regular season with the highest steals per game average among qualified players. If the leader is not a listed player, the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

To qualify, a player must meet the NBA's minimum requirements for its official 2026-27 regular-season per-game leaderboard (a player who appears in at least 58 regular-season games qualifies), applied exactly as reflected on NBA.com/stats. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

In the event of a tie for the highest steals per game average, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player with more total steals during the 2026-27 NBA regular season. If a tie still persists, each tied player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, the outcome shall be determined using available NBA statistics for completed games, with leaderboard qualification applied as the NBA applies it to the shortened season.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or it is unclear which player led the NBA in steals per game within that timeframe, each listed player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
markets.question: Will Jalen Johnson lead the NBA in steals per game in 2026-27?

markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed company announces that it has paused or will pause all training of AI models over safety, alignment, or security concerns by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A full training pause means the company halts all training for its AI models, including pre-training, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning, across the company. Pauses limited to particular models, training methods, training environments, or teams will not qualify. A full pause of any stated duration qualifies. Continued deployment or serving of existing models does not prevent a pause from qualifying.

A qualifying announcement must be made through the listed company's official channels or by an authorized representative acting in an official capacity, and must state that all training has been or will be paused. The company must itself attribute the pause, at least in part, to safety, alignment, or security concerns. Statements that describe slowing development, pausing some training, or considering a pause will not qualify.

If a qualifying announcement is made within this market's timeframe, this market will resolve to "Yes" regardless of whether the pause is actually carried out, is later modified or withdrawn, or training later resumes. The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the listed company; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
The 2026 midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the US State gubernatorial race which has the smallest margin of victory. 

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For elections that include runoffs, ranked-choice, or other multi-round elections, the relevant margin of victory will be that of the round in which the winner is determined. 

If two state margins of victory are identical, this market will resolve to the tied state whose name comes first alphabetically.

This market will consider all regular and special gubernatorial elections that are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026. 

For the purposes of this market, US State is defined to exclude territories, the District of Columbia, and any other subdivision that is not a state. 

The resolution source for this market will be a compilation of all of the relevant state election authorities responsible for certifying statewide elections, however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
The 2026 NJ-06 House election is currently expected to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

The "margin of victory" is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For purposes of this market, candidates nominated by the Democratic & Republican Parties will represent the options for "Democrat" and "Republican," respectively. Independent candidates will not represent options for either party. The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the 2026 NJ-06 House election as published by the state electoral authority responsible for certifying the results of the election; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

If a tie still persists, this market will resolve in favor of the team with a higher average yards per return during the 2026-27 NFL regular season. markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at King Abdulaziz International Airport (OEJN) on 8 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for King Abdulaziz International Airport (OEJN) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for King Abdulaziz International Airport (OEJN) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=OEJN&format=raw&date=2026-11-09T00:00:00Z&hours=30

T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Chaudhary Charan Singh Intl Airport (VILK) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=VILK&format=raw&date=2026-11-07T21:30:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Wuhan Tianhe International Airport (ZHHH) on 7 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Wuhan Tianhe International Airport (ZHHH) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Wuhan Tianhe International Airport (ZHHH) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=ZHHH&format=raw&date=2026-11-07T19:00:00Z&hours=30

For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Ninoy Aquino International Airport (RPLL) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=RPLL&format=raw&date=2026-11-07T19:00:00Z&hours=30

If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed bank fails between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

For the purposes of this market, the listed bank will be considered to have “failed” if any of the following occurs under the bank’s applicable legal or regulatory framework, within the listed date range:

- The listed bank’s primary banking regulator formally declares the institution insolvent or non-viable, or withdraws or revokes the bank’s license or authorization, and such determination initiates or directly results in resolution, liquidation, wind-down, or transfer actions.
- The listed bank enters a court-ordered liquidation, statutory resolution regime, or regulator-mandated wind-down, including the use of resolution tools such as bail-ins, forced asset transfers, or the establishment of a bridge bank.
- A government or resolution authority intervenes in a manner that wipes out or subordinates existing equity of the listed bank and transfers effective control of the bank to the state or a designated resolution authority, with continued operations dependent on official intervention.
- The listed bank publicly defaults on a payment obligation, including derivatives margin, repo, or physical commodity delivery, and such default is formally acknowledged by the bank’s primary regulator or resolution authority and directly results in the initiation of resolution, liquidation, license withdrawal, or regulator-mandated transfer of the bank.
- The listed bank is subject to a compulsory merger, acquisition, or transfer of all or substantially all of its assets and liabilities ordered or directed by its primary banking regulator or resolution authority due to the bank’s financial condition or to prevent failure, regardless of whether a formal insolvency declaration or immediate equity wipeout is publicly announced at the time of transfer.

If there is a potential failure of the listed bank within this market’s date range and a qualifying regulatory or court action has occurred but has not yet been fully published by the relevant authority, this market may remain open until April 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET to allow for confirmation. If no qualifying failure is confirmed by that date, this market will resolve to “No.”

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements, filings, or actions by the listed bank’s primary banking regulator or resolution authority; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No". Price action before this market’s creation will not be considered.

For CME Gold (GC) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (February, April, June, August, October, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month changes automatically on the contract's First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Gold (GC) futures.  If the official settlement price for any relevant trading day has not been published on the CME Group website within 72 hours of the final trading day (ET) of the specified period, the market will resolve based on the settlement prices published through all CME channels up to that point.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".
